issues.legal_issue: A disabled landlord’s share in a joint family is not separated by metes and bounds for purposes of postponing a tenant’s purchase right when the partition covers only agricultural land and other joint family assets remain undivided.
material_facts: In both appeals, a landlord was a widow or minor who was treated as a person with a disability under the Act, and at least one other joint-family member was outside the disabled categories.
The families owned agricultural land and other assets. The partitions relied on by the landlords covered agricultural land only, while other family assets remained joint and undivided.
The tenants claimed the statutory right to purchase the tenanted land, and the landlords claimed that the partition brought them within the protective proviso.

The Court proceeded on the assumption that the partitions occurred within the relevant period and held that the agricultural-land-only partitions did not satisfy the proviso. The tenants’ purchase rights were therefore upheld.
issues.conclusion: The proviso did not postpone the tenants’ purchase rights because the disabled landlords’ shares had not been separated from all joint family property; the appeals were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 32 and 32F(1)(a) of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1948, a disabled landlord may obtain the statutory postponement of a tenant’s purchase right only if the proviso’s requirements are met. The disabled person’s share must be separated by metes and bounds from the entire joint family property, not merely from its agricultural land. The Mamlatdar must also be satisfied that the disabled person’s share in the land is proportionate to that person’s share in the entire joint family property and is not larger. Section 32G concerns the proceeding to determine the purchase price. The Court relied on no earlier cases.

rule.if: tenancy_purchase_dispute and disabled_landlord_in_joint_family and another_member_outside_disability_group and partition_confined_to_agricultural_land and other_joint_family_assets_remain_undivided

predicates.tenancy_purchase_dispute: A tenant claims a statutory right to purchase land, and the landlord contests whether that right is postponed.
predicates.disabled_landlord_in_joint_family: A landlord who belongs to a legally recognized disabled category is a member of a joint family that owns the land.
predicates.another_member_outside_disability_group: At least one other member of the joint family does not belong to the disabled categories.
predicates.partition_confined_to_agricultural_land: The family partition separates agricultural land but does not separate all property held jointly by the family.
predicates.other_joint_family_assets_remain_undivid: Assets of the joint family other than the agricultural land remain jointly held.

issues.definition: When a tenant claims a purchase right and a disabled landlord in a joint family relies on a partition limited to agricultural land while other family assets remain undivided, the tenant’s purchase right is not postponed.
